lines.4da1b56e5a9acc68: Hello, astronaut! Welcome to Arcadia, our base on the Moon. I'm your station assistant, and I'll help you all along.
lines.3f750316e4f7c9f4: Before we start, what would you like to know?
lines.f6fb59d916836133: I'm the base's helper robot. I watch the air, the power and the water, and I explain everything you need.
lines.34ba73f2fd268a8c: We're near the Moon's equator, in the Sea of Tranquility, not far from where Apollo 11 landed in 1969. From here, the Earth never moves: it hangs high in the sky, day and night!
lines.ce3ddeb6d002e00c: I like your energy! Just one quick question first.
lines.e6dc31f2adefe214: There is no air outside on the Moon. What does the crew need most to stay alive here?
lines.4b2cede7a10bb4b1: Yes! We make our own air, and we must not waste it.
lines.a93114a0f54e1ece: The Moon has plenty of dust, but nobody can breathe it.
lines.cf61b6cfd14cbaad: Music is nice, but it will not keep us alive!
lines.cdde30acfec7205e: Watch three gauges on your dashboard: air, power and water. Every job uses some of them, so think before you act.
lines.8496dea7290624b1: Today we have two jobs. The robot must dig regolith, the dust and broken rock that covers the Moon. And our 3D printer must be tuned, so it can turn that regolith into bricks!
lines.51066da195750f5f: You are the commander. What do you want to start with?
lines.b3869385b0dd47eb: Good idea: a well-tuned printer wastes less regolith.
lines.7881be907d879636: The robot must bring 50 kg of regolith to the base. Before you drive it, a quick lesson at the academy!
lines.14e33ef4a6aa376a: Welcome to the academy! Our robot is based on RASSOR, a real NASA digging robot. Its two drums spin in opposite directions.
lines.b62b59de8719bfd8: Why two drums? On the Moon you weigh six times less than on Earth. One drum would push the light robot away; two opposite drums cancel each other's push.
lines.fa06204839e82942: In 2009, NASA crashed the LCROSS rocket stage into a dark crater near the south pole. The cloud it raised contained water ice! Our ground here holds much less, but our drums can still dig a little out.
lines.470d0856949ecb34: Why is ice in the regolith so precious for the base?
lines.981f012d602caefb: Right! With electricity we split water into oxygen to breathe and hydrogen.
lines.2b52817760f6cce5: Fridges are easy here. The ice is much more useful: it is water, and water gives oxygen.
lines.04c241841daae132: To drive: the arrow keys, or W A S D (Z Q S D on a French keyboard). In the yellow zone, hold Space to dig. In the red zone, hold Space to unload.
lines.7c76fcb24a1c9e78: You drive the robot from inside the base, by remote control. Careful: rolling and spinning the drums drain its battery, and it cannot recharge today. Plan your moves!
lines.b1b9e9d2c1611280: Our 3D printer melts regolith into bricks with a laser beam. Before it can print, its laser must be aimed just right.
lines.c42cbb2717afd509: Why make bricks here instead of bringing them from Earth?
lines.8fedc6d277499cc0: Exactly! Every kilogram sent to the Moon costs a lot. Regolith is already here.
lines.0da9c6ba607f2250: Not really. The real reason: rockets can carry only a little, and regolith is free here.
lines.30ab47a26798e3d4: NASA is testing machines that heat regolith until its grains stick together, to build landing pads and walls on the Moon.
lines.723f1f380c3b3986: Our printer does it with a laser. Mirrors guide the beam to the right spot, like light bouncing off a bathroom mirror.
lines.b65e59e9a34c8f5b: What happens if the printer is badly tuned?
lines.184d7ca0fe9779d2: Yes! A badly aimed laser melts the wrong spots, so fewer bricks come out.
lines.a781f9e5c6a8324f: No, the opposite: a badly aimed laser wastes regolith.
lines.7c85d0a344faaf15: Flip the mirrors to guide the beam to every target. Each flip uses the laser, so think before you flip!
lines.4e027c2c0ccead22: Good morning, commander! Day two. Today, you decide what the crew works on.
lines.13d14f5099182b5e: Every job costs bricks, power or water. Some jobs are too expensive for now: you will see them greyed out, with what is missing.
lines.9090ae659a47edb3: Mission control advises a shelter. What could the crew need to hide from on the Moon?
lines.498bd6c84e442926: Yes! The Sun sometimes throws out a storm of fast particles. On the Moon, there is no air to stop them.
lines.f5be040c2f796366: There is no rain on the Moon: there is no air at all. The danger comes from the Sun.
lines.c548f592e4e3fa30: Nothing lives on the Moon. The danger comes from the Sun.
lines.6d5044272d6d9e5d: Now look at the plan, and choose what you want to do today.
lines.eb197e4d100a446b: We build the shelter with the bricks the printer made. Thick walls slow down the Sun's particles.
lines.e7c95bb15a899e8f: Water and materials full of hydrogen block radiation well. That is why space shelters use them.
lines.833417868c51f8e4: On NASA's Orion spacecraft, if a solar storm comes, the crew builds a shelter with bags of food and water, and hides inside.
lines.6870329026086c12: Our crane lifts the bricks into place. Hang every weight on the crane arm and keep the arm level. Fewer moves, fewer bricks wasted!
lines.27ce8a8693cedd3c: Today we plant seeds in the glass dome, our greenhouse outside the base. Plants give us food, and even a little oxygen!
lines.5f480899b580b2df: Seeds need water to grow. Ours comes from the ice the robot dug out of the regolith.
lines.0eee3254e103b79e: In 2015, NASA astronauts ate lettuce they grew in space. It grew in a small plant box on the space station.
lines.60a16277921d5f15: Plants cannot do everything yet. To make the oxygen of just one astronaut, you would need a garden as big as a classroom!
lines.46d135a079437a1e: What do our seeds need to grow on the Moon?
lines.83c8b9ca061c905c: Yes! The dome lets the sunlight in and keeps the plants warm. We bring the water.
lines.2995ede164ca4e9f: Moon dust alone is not enough. Like on Earth, plants need water, light and warmth.
lines.113c80044536d7ae: Put on your suit, go out through the airlock and walk to the glass dome. Outside, your suit uses oxygen, so do not wander too long!
lines.1018c9737b4b0581: At the dome, turn the pipes so the water flows to the seeds. Every extra turn lets a little water leak: think before you turn!
lines.bf208595c498d04b: What a start! The base has bricks, and the crew knows how to protect itself.
lines.ca2849ad90cc3ca3: New missions are on their way. Until then, you can start a new game and try to use even less air and power!
lines.55116adace6e86d4: Mission accomplished, and you saved the base resources. Great planning!
lines.55194b8135d48efb: Your suit ran low, so the crew brought you back inside. Next time, watch your oxygen and battery and come back earlier.
lines.fbbcc1e1f7b44cfb: Real astronauts plan every move, because air and power are precious far from Earth.
lines.de65763495e8612a: Mission accomplished, but it cost the base a lot.
lines.7576f86a397e0f54: Most of the power went into driving and digging. Fewer moves and fuller loads between the yellow and red zones save the robot battery.
lines.60a31c32427d51b0: The mission is not finished this time. That is okay: let us see what happened.
lines.bd789e4c26e05a2e: Every mirror flip used the laser, and a rough tuning means fewer bricks. Think about the beam path before flipping.
lines.9848f54a651466ac: The shelter is finished, with no brick wasted. The crew has a safe place now.
lines.fdd44b4c6a60639a: The shelter is finished, but 2 bricks were wasted. Fewer moves on the crane save bricks.
lines.125919f78252c0c5: The shelter is not finished, and 2 bricks were lost. Without it, the crew has nowhere safe to hide.
lines.1ea8de5f20541679: The seeds got no water this time, so nothing will grow yet.
lines.655c18eb36fcc2ad: The printer starts. Bricks will help us build a shelter. Tonight the crew still breathes, drinks, eats and uses power: 5 points of air, water, food and power.
lines.9bd23b119910f95f: We save power, but we will have no bricks tomorrow. Tonight the crew still breathes, drinks, eats and uses power: 5 points of air, water, food and power.
lines.6c4863948da0f9f2: The day's work is done. Tonight the crew still breathes, drinks, eats and uses power: 5 points of air, water, food and power.
lines.fa4fa0b9f3e5293f: Base to commander, do you copy? I know it might feel like a game. But it's not completely one. Look up: the Earth is high in the sky. From our base, it stays right there, day and night.
lines.bd089d50b717bad6: Good morning, commander! Welcome to the Moon base. Take a walk around the base to see how it works. When you are ready, come to the station dashboard to start your mission.
lines.fd2098d05d8a8c72: Suit on, commander! Go out through the airlock and walk to the glass dome. Follow the green light!
lines.1fa9965f4df39d15: That is enough regolith! Drive to the red zone and hold Space to unload it.
lines.ef9a86a4ecdcfd96: Well done, the regolith is at the base! Now press E to leave the robot and save its battery.
